digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and digest history storage
propositions: Physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, TICKET_DIGEST events causes git rename-detection conflicts across clones despite appearing safe locally

Current read strategy in overlap/queue.py opens every matching file (4,977 opens per full-store reduce) causing 20ms budget overruns; newest-first suffix read reduces opens to 1,658 without requiring deletion
Deletion-based retention schemes violate invariant I1 (docs/concurrency.md) and reclaim zero repository space since blobs remain in git history
Read-only suffix-lazy design preserves every committed UUID event unchanged, maintains I1, and is merge-safe by construction since two clones produce identical behavior
The design bounds per-ticket read cost to O(dirents) plus 3+k file opens for reduce_ticket and c opens for claim arbitration, with no term growing as a function of total history
